players.product: AI-Native Cloud: inference cloud (Inference Engine, serverless inference) and GPU Droplets on NVIDIA HGX and AMD Instinct GPUs, integrated with its Core Cloud

quarterly_data.signal: Agent platform (CEO): last week DigitalOcean announced a new product called Agent Harness, Open Harness Runtime, which lets customers bring any agent harness (Hermes, Codex, OpenClaw) onto its platform while DigitalOcean runs the agent in a secure sandbox and handles observability and life-cycle management; sandboxes hydrate in hundreds of milliseconds and rehydrate in less than 100 milliseconds, versus multiple minutes for virtual machines, and customers pay only for CPU cycles consumed. CEO: DigitalOcean now has 680,000 customers; the token business launched 'probably 120 days' ago and already has '6,000, 7,000 customers'. Go-to-market: on top of product-led growth it is increasing direct customer acquisition with the top '300, 500 AI-native companies' and has two forward-deployed engineering (FDE) organizations. CEO: the higher up the stack customers consume (agent runtimes, storage, databases), the more it looks like software economics rather than GPU economics.
quarterly_data.figure: 680,000 customers; token business 6,000-7,000 customers in about 120 days; sandbox rehydration less than 100 milliseconds

quarterly_data.signal: GPU pricing and mix (management): CFO: very little of DigitalOcean's revenue is under long-term contract, so it raises prices on renewal - including on some of its small bare-metal base - or migrates those customers onto its inference services. CEO: spot instances launched a few weeks ago and capacity placed on demand or spot 'is gone' within the minute; H100 prices are going up again - DigitalOcean saw it 3 weeks ago because its fungible on-demand H100 fleet goes 'even before we have them available'. As the year end approaches it is doing fewer and fewer GPU-as-a-service deals, shifting to what it calls elastic compute (serverless inferencing, on-demand and spot) to maximize fleet utilization and yield per megawatt. CEO: surge or scarcity-based GPU pricing 'is a temporary spike', while token flow and agent flow are the durable value streams.

Capacity sourcing (CFO): 'we do not play the gigawatt game, we play the megawatt game' - DigitalOcean looks for tens and 20s of megawatts or smaller from tier 1 data center operators, which de-risks execution; the 3 data centers it turned on this year were all turned on ahead of time and are ramping well. As it seeks incremental capacity it will take bigger locations than it has looked at so far, and says it fares favorably with data center providers because it is profitable and generates cash, unlike other neoclouds. CFO: it could get really big really quickly by pursuing training workloads or bare-metal contracts but would sacrifice what makes it different; its aspiration is to get materially larger with software-oriented, inference-oriented capacity that has similar return characteristics.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 data centers turned on in 2026, all ahead of time

quarterly_data.signal: Returns and capex per megawatt (CFO): DigitalOcean has not changed its view of acceptable return on investment or payback; it underwrites new data centers and GPU investments with very conservative revenue assumptions that assume price compression ('we have been wrong, right? Prices have been going up') and targets paybacks in 'the 3-ish year kind of a range'. CapEx per megawatt is increasing, partly because component costs are going up but mainly because newer generations of NVIDIA and AMD gear carry much more token capacity and cost more per megawatt, while the ARR per megawatt they generate also continues to go up. CFO: Core Cloud is the highest-margin part of the business, at the roughly 70% gross margins of the pre-AI business.
quarterly_data.figure: payback target 3-ish year range; Core Cloud 70% gross margins

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 outlook (CFO): more information on the outlook will come in November with earnings. Since the 50%+ 2027 growth outlook was given, DigitalOcean has signed nine-figure deals that give visibility, secured 20 megawatts of incremental capacity, launched the token business and raised the exit growth outlook for this year to 35% plus; data center capacity is coming on on time or ahead of schedule and prices are going up, not down. CFO: 'If you start at 35 and you average 50, what do you end at? You end at something north of 50 by the end of next year.'
